note: Terms the entries use without defining them. Each definition says what the word means, never what a ruling is, and follows the sense the entry itself gives it. 'source' names a work the seed already cites or the entry that explains the term. 'aliases' are other spellings matched in the text.

terms.definition: Turning back. The classical jurists' word for leaving Islam after professing it, from the Arabic root r-d-d.
Turning back, from the same root as irtidad. Also the name of the wars fought against armed secession from the early Muslim polity.
terms.source: M. Hamidullah, The Muslim Conduct of State, p. 6, para. 330.

terms.definition: Respite: God's deferral of punishment, so that a wrongdoer is not seized at once.
Maintenance: a husband's obligation to provide for his wife and children, and where required for other dependants.
terms.source: The standard treatments in the four Sunni schools, as cited in The inheritance shares.

terms.definition: The marriage gift a husband gives his wife. It is her own property, and he has no claim on it.
Shame: a family's reputation, guarded by keeping a wrong inside the house. A cultural pattern, not a teaching of the religion.
terms.source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Mazalim, on restraining the one who wrongs.

terms.definition: Malay for the head-cover worn by Muslim women.
Fixed prescribed penalties for a small number of offences. The classical jurists reserved them to constituted authority.
Insolence, or a serious breach of the marital bond, as the jurists used the word in reading Qur'an 4:34.
Assent: the heart's inward affirmation, which faith requires.
Faith: belief held with the heart's assent. No registry can issue it or revoke it.
The chain of transmitters through whom a hadith reached the one who recorded it.
The text of a hadith report, as distinct from its chain of transmission.
Stopped: a report traced to a Companion and not attributed to the Prophet.
terms.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 3849, discussed in The monkeys report.

terms.definition: Severed: a report that stops at a Successor, a Muslim of the generation after the Companions, and is not attributed to the Prophet.
terms.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 3849, discussed in The monkeys report.

terms.definition: The sciences of hadith: the disciplines that test reports by their chain and their text, and grade them.
Jurisprudence: the human work of deriving and applying rulings from the sources.
Legal theory: the principles by which rulings are derived.
terms.source: The state of the Muslims (this site).

terms.definition: Creed: the articles of belief.
terms.source: The state of the Muslims (this site).

terms.definition: Theological disputation: the discipline that argued doctrine in public, by reason.
terms.source: Ibn Rushd, Tahafut al-Tahafut, replying to al-Ghazali's Tahafut al-Falasifah.

terms.definition: Inimitability: the doctrine that the Qur'an cannot be matched, argued from its language and composition.
terms.source: Abu Bakr al-Baqillani, I'jaz al-Qur'an; Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani, Dala'il al-I'jaz.

terms.definition: The challenge: the Qur'an's invitation to produce something like it.
Composition: the ordering of words and meanings that al-Jurjani held to be the ground of the Qur'an's inimitability.
A covenant of protection extended to a non-Muslim community, with enforceable content: life, property and places of worship.
A member of a non-Muslim community living under the dhimma.
A tax on free adult non-Muslim men of means living under the dhimma. Muslims paid zakat in its place.
The obligatory alms Muslims pay from their wealth, to set categories of recipient.
Struggle or exertion, from jahada. It is not a synonym for armed combat.
terms.source: Hadith: the mujahid is the one who performs jihad against his own self.

terms.definition: Fighting; armed combat. Related to jihad, and not the same word.
One who rejects the truth. It describes a position taken, and is not a synonym for non-Muslim.
People whom the message has not reached. God does not punish before a message has reached a person.
Expiation: the prescribed remedy for certain wrongs, such as a broken oath or a broken fast, which often meant freeing a slave.
A contract by which a slave bought his own freedom.
A woman who bore her master's child. She could not be sold, and was free at his death.
Usury: interest taken on a loan.
The fixed shares of Islamic inheritance law.
Conjugal availability, as the classical jurists discussed it within marriage.
terms.source: Marital consent and the rape charge (this site).

terms.definition: God-consciousness: the ground on which the Qur'an distinguishes one person from another.
Reviling the Prophet. Classical law held it an offence, and the schools differed on its treatment.
Modesty, as a virtue of character asked of men and women alike.
A duty binding on each individual person, including the knowledge every person owes.
terms.source: Syed Muhammad Naquib al-Attas, Islam and Secularism, p. 113.

terms.definition: A collective duty, discharged for all when enough of the community takes it up, such as the technical and professional knowledge a society needs.
terms.source: Syed Muhammad Naquib al-Attas, Islam and Secularism, p. 113.

terms.definition: A report of what the Prophet said, did or approved, carried by a chain of narrators from the one who witnessed it.
The Prophet's practice and teaching, as the reports preserve it. With the Qur'an, it is the ground of the law.
terms.source: The slide from hadith to nothing (this site).

terms.definition: Abrogation: the replacement of an earlier ruling by a later one, as the jurists used the word.
terms.source: Abrogation and the edited book (this site).

terms.definition: The community of Muslims as a whole, across every country, language and school.
The path of law and ethics drawn from the Qur'an and the Sunnah. Syariah is the Malay spelling, and a Syariah court is a state court that applies it to Muslims.
A legal opinion a qualified scholar gives in answer to a question. It is advice, and not the judgment of a court.
Sound: the highest grade of hadith, given to a report whose chain is unbroken, whose narrators are reliable, and which carries no hidden defect.
Of the majority tradition in Islam, which follows the Sunnah as the Companions as a whole transmitted it.
Of the Shi'a, the tradition which holds that leadership after the Prophet passed to 'Ali and the imams of his line.
terms.source: Blasphemy and the Rushdie case (this site).

terms.definition: Of the school of law named after Abu Hanifa, who died in 150 AH. One of the four Sunni schools.
Of the school of law named after Malik ibn Anas, who died in 179 AH. One of the four Sunni schools.
Of the school of law named after Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, who died in 204 AH. One of the four Sunni schools.
Of the school of law named after Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who died in 241 AH. One of the four Sunni schools.
Of the literalist school of law, which held to the plain sense of the texts and rejected analogy. Ibn Hazm is its best-known jurist.
A school of theology that argued doctrine from reason, and held that human beings create their own acts.
terms.source: Decree and the charge of fatalism (this site).

terms.definition: Of the school of theology that followed Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who died in 324 AH, and became the majority Sunni creed.
terms.source: Decree and the charge of fatalism (this site).

terms.definition: Of the school of theology that followed Abu Mansur al-Maturidi, who died in 333 AH. The second Sunni school of creed, followed widely by Hanafis.
terms.source: Decree and the charge of fatalism (this site).

terms.definition: The cube-shaped sanctuary at the centre of the Sacred Mosque in Makka, which Muslims face in prayer.
Circling the Ka'bah seven times, a rite of the pilgrimage.
A festival. Muslims keep two: one at the end of Ramadan, and one at the close of the pilgrimage.
terms.source: Music, images, and the schools (this site).

terms.definition: The one who gives the call to prayer.
The duty of commanding right and forbidding wrong, and the office that carried it out in markets and public places.
terms.source: Modesty and the morality police (this site).

terms.definition: The officer who held the hisbah: an inspector of weights, measures, trade and public conduct in the market.
terms.source: Modesty and the morality police (this site).

terms.definition: The sharia enforcement agency of the Indonesian province of Aceh.
terms.source: Modesty and the morality police (this site).

terms.definition: The natural disposition with which every person is born.
A Zoroastrian: a follower of the old religion of Persia, called majus in Arabic.
A frame drum, played by hand.
terms.source: Music, images, and the schools (this site).

terms.definition: Musical instruments. The lexicographers applied the word to stringed and other played instruments.
Compulsion: the power some classical schools gave a father to contract the marriage of a daughter who had never married, without her express consent.
What is known to be right: the decent and customary standard. Bil-ma'ruf means with kindness, or according to what is fair.
A Successor: a Muslim of the generation after the Companions, who met at least one of them.
Ignorance: the name for Arabia before Islam.
The city in western Arabia where the Prophet was born and where the Ka'bah stands.
terms.source: Decree and the charge of fatalism (this site).

terms.definition: Revealed at Makka, before the Prophet's emigration to Madinah in 622.
terms.source: Abrogation and the edited book (this site).

terms.definition: Revealed at Madinah, after the Prophet's emigration there in 622.
terms.source: Abrogation and the edited book (this site).

terms.definition: A hadith collection arranged by subject, which records the opinions of Companions and Successors beside the Prophet's words. That of 'Abd al-Razzaq, who died in 211 AH, is among the earliest.
The collection of hadith and Madinan legal practice compiled by Malik ibn Anas, who died in 179 AH.
Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din, The Revival of the Religious Sciences: al-Ghazali's work on law, worship and the inner life.
terms.source: Music, images, and the schools (this site).

terms.definition: One who performs jihad, in any of its senses.
He strove, or exerted himself: the verb from which the word jihad is formed.
Forbidden: the category of acts the law prohibits.
No harm, and no harming in return: a saying of the Prophet that the jurists took as a governing maxim.
terms.source: Sunan Ibn Majah 2340; graded sahih by al-Albani.

terms.definition: Not severe: the Prophet's qualifier, in the Farewell Sermon, on the striking named in Qur'an 4:34.
The Prophet's address to the pilgrims at 'Arafa in 10 AH (632), months before his death.
A chapter of the Qur'an. There are 114.
A hill north of Madinah, and the battle fought below it in 3 AH (625), which left many Muslim households without men.
The mosque and university in Cairo, founded in 970, and one of the leading centres of Sunni learning.
Sahih al-Bukhari, the hadith collection of Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari, who died in 256 AH. Sunnis hold it the most reliable of the collections.
Sunan Abu Dawud, a collection of hadith on law compiled by Abu Dawud al-Sijistani, who died in 275 AH. One of the six canonical books.
Sunan Ibn Majah, a hadith collection compiled by Ibn Majah al-Qazwini, who died in 273 AH. The last of the six canonical books.
